arguments.query: Which candidate is the best next bounded, offline, evidence-producing investigation for the Ford Racing 2 PS2 reverse-engineering effort, given: milestone #2 is done and out-of-scope items (audio codec, mesh geometry, full PTG, UI/text grammar) are explicitly separate investigations; the user forbids new debugger windows or focus stealing; findings must be testable against the real corpus with counterexamples, not asserted from other games?

candidates.text: Audio payload codec. Measured offline just now over the real corpus: all 27 .msb banks (193+ descriptor spans) have every span length a multiple of 16, first 16-byte block all zero, last block flags bit0 (end) set, and 0.000 of 16-byte blocks violate the PS-ADPCM rule filter<=4 / shift<=12 / flags<=7. Control files (.ps2, .ptg, .dat) violate filter<=4 in 39-96% of blocks. 20 .mib music files (5-14 MB) also have 0.000 violations; their .mih words are [64, X, 2, 44100, 32768, N]. Next step: decode to PCM offline with an independent implementation, test falsifiers (clipping rate, loop/end flag positions, stereo interleave 0x8000 channel consistency, duration vs mih field), and cross-check against EE/IOP code. No emulator window needed.

Additional PTG sprite profiles. Of 548 PTG files only 16 satisfy the current gear-sprite profile; 505 fail with 'sprite dimensions exceed stride or are empty', 24 with 'unsupported sprite pattern table', 3 with 'unsupported sprite header profile'. The headers of the 505 are unprobed. Purely static, offline, cheap; decoded pixels could be hashed and visually checked by the user only for gear glyphs.

Model geometry and the unresolved leading count of the 56 .ps2 model trees (e.g. 49COUPE leading_count=431, file 1,146,656 bytes; FORDGT count noted as 643). Only the name tree is decoded; vertex/primitive data is retained by hash. Needs hypothesis search on binary layouts plus consumer code in the EE ELF (and likely VU1 microcode). Larger, more speculative, but central to full game reverse engineering.

Downstream consumer analysis: trace what EE/IOP/VU code does with loaded buffers (sound upload to SPU2, texture upload via GIF, model draw via VU1). 3446 functions are inventoried; loader stages are mapped, consumers beyond the loader return sites are not. Static-only analysis feasible; large scope and no existing target definition.

Text/config grammars: 216 .dat, 45 .ui, 16 .cfg, 5 .mbf plus translation tables tlate_*.dat. Text-like, cheap to probe offline; previous notes mention ':TYPE' and '//' comments. Not required by milestone #2.
Build a mac_arm_64 Ghidra decompiler natively (gradle + clang) so C pseudocode is available. Heavy setup, produces no new asset-format evidence by itself; issue #2 calls it a follow-up.

New PCSX2 runtime captures of more asset types. The existing capture path opens debugger windows and takes desktop focus, which the user explicitly complained about and forbade repeating; no verified windowless mode exists.

Housekeeping with deterministic content: commit the verified .DS_Store verifier fix, reconcile stale project-map prose (says no milestones/child tickets) with native sub-issue data, record completion criteria. Required but yields no new reverse-engineering knowledge.

Ask the user whether the broader finish line is bounded asset formats only, or includes mesh/VU/render reconstruction. The handoff says to resolve material scope ambiguity with one focused question while continuing independent inspection.
